It was a nice bulltrap. The support level around 3144 was basically already taken out after the spike below, so the move up into the supply area provided low risk entries for the big players, and huge rewards. As you marked, this was a multiple R:R trade if taken at "real" supply.

DrSwing, you could have taken the entry off lower timeframes after we engulfed the "base" from the HTF supply retest at S/R flip. It looks scary to enter short there because of the previous "bull bar", but in fact, there was no buy level because of the spike down clearing path for further move.

Take a look at this stretched EURUSD analysis (m5 chart) - you have to right click and expand to read comments

So I've been taking a look at price action around news, and with NFP (non farm payroll) out today it was the perfect test bed. The first chart were my thoughts on the EUR/USD well before news time. This is pretty much how I view trades. After the engulf south, where is price going to retrace to, so that I can enter a short? But NFP adds a little spice to things!! Now I didn't trade this, I just made a plan and watched how it unfolded or unravelled:).

The plan was to enter a TT of the lower zone with the stoploss hidden behind the upper zone, as this should cover any FO.

The M15 chart below is how it played out. I have noticed that just before news the pros push price beyond levels to provide liquidity for their reversals.

posts.t:
DrSwing wrote: I had a trade last week (posted in my journal) where I got stopped out (faked out) by 5pips before price went in my direction. Price then just smashed back down without any retrace to allow me to re-enter the move. On post analysis I was happy with the setup and just put it down to a trade that didn't work, and moved on........... Or so I had thought, but I found myself thinking that this could happen again on my next swing, since I didn't have a reason as to why it had happened!! We are usually scared of things that we don't understand. Knowing that this would lead to indecision and hesitancy in my future shot making, I set about analysing FOs (fake outs).

Just for clarity, I'll be talking about:

S/D - Supply/Demand SUP - Supply D - Demand S/R - Support Resistance Swap - Suport becomes resistance and vice versa ENG - Engulf

FTR - Failure To Return FTB - First Time Back FO - Fake Out FL - Flag Limit

Using a Weekly chart of the AUD/USD I've marked one FO pattern in red and the other FO in blue

I've kept all markings on the chart to a minimum for clarity.

Basically I'm saying here that the area between an FTR and the price zone that it failed to returned to, is a potential FO zone. This FO zone needs to be narrow to have potential, as the pros have to be able to drive price beyond the FTR to the S/D level.

To me an FTR can relate to any important zone, whether it be S/D, S/R, Swap or FL. The red pattern has an S/R - FTR FO zone and the blue pattern has an S/D -FTR FO zone. FOs provide large liquidity for the pros to buy/sell into and so they can lead to a large move in price. Coast to coast type of thing.

Hmm, makes sense. The only thing that I wonder is that both times there was a FTR and a retrace that you labeled FTB. That means that when price entered the third time for the FO price might have just been going to the next zone as it was the third attempt.

Makes sense? I don't know, I am just adding a comment to your post. I wish there was a way to know if price was going to fake out or not. It makes your stop larger when you have to include two levels into one.

5pips DrSwing نوشت: هفتهٔ گذشته معامله‌ای داشتم (در ژورنالم پست شده) که 5 پیپ استاپ شدم (فیک‌اوت) و بعد قیمت در جهت من رفت. بعد قیمت بدون هیچ ریتریسی که اجازهٔ ورود دوباره به حرکت را بدهد، به‌شدت به پایین کوبید. در تحلیل بعدی از ستاپ راضی بودم و فقط آن را یک معاملهٔ کارنکرده گذاشتم و رد شدم………… یا حداقل خودم فکر می‌کردم. اما دیدم ذهنم مشغول این است که این می‌تواند در سوینگ بعدی هم تکرار شود، چون دلیلی برایش نداشتم!! ما معمولاً از چیزی که نمی‌فهمیم می‌ترسیم. با دانستن اینکه این به تردید و تعلل در ضربه‌های بعدی‌ام منجر می‌شود، شروع کردم به تحلیل FO (فیک‌اوت).

برای روشنی، دربارهٔ این‌ها حرف می‌زنم:

S/D - عرضه/تقاضا SUP - عرضه D - تقاضا S/R - حمایت و مقاومت Swap - حمایت تبدیل به مقاومت و برعکس ENG - اینگالف

FTR - شکست در بازگشت FTB - اولین بازگشت FO - فیک‌اوت FL - حد فلگ

با استفاده از چارت هفتگی AUD/USD، یک الگوی FO را قرمز و دیگری را آبی علامت زده‌ام

همهٔ علامت‌گذاری‌ها را برای روشنی در چارت حداقل نگه داشته‌ام.

اساساً می‌گویم اینجا که ناحیهٔ بین یک FTR و ناحیهٔ قیمتی‌ای که قیمت نتوانست به آن برگردد، یک ناحیهٔ FO بالقوه است. این ناحیهٔ FO باید باریک باشد تا بالقوه باشد، چون حرفه‌ای‌ها باید بتوانند قیمت را فراتر از FTR تا سطح S/D ببرند.

برای من FTR می‌تواند به هر ناحیهٔ مهمی مربوط باشد، چه S/D، چه S/R، چه Swap یا FL. الگوی قرمز یک ناحیهٔ FO روی S/R - FTR دارد و الگوی آبی ناحیهٔ FO روی S/D - FTR. FO‌ها لیکوییدیتی زیادی برای خرید/فروش حرفه‌ای‌ها فراهم می‌کنند و بنابراین می‌توانند به حرکت بزرگ قیمت منجر شوند. یعنی یک حرکت «از ساحل به ساحل».

هومم، منطقی است. فقط چیزی که برایم سؤال است این است که هر دو بار یک FTR و یک برگشت بود که FTB نامیدی. یعنی وقتی قیمت بار سوم برای FO وارد شد، ممکن بود فقط به ناحیهٔ بعدی می‌رفت چون تلاش سوم بود.

منطقی است؟ نمی‌دانم، فقط دارم به پستت کامنت می‌گذارم. ای کاش راهی بود که بفهمیم قیمت فیک‌اوت می‌کند یا نه. وقتی مجبوری دو سطح را در یکی حساب کنی، استاپت بزرگ‌تر می‌شود.

Nice engulf trade Dr. Swing.

Perfect place to look for engulf.

Here is some TP places on your chart. What I would say to you is, follow the trade on H1 and keep marking the swing lows on the way up. Moment you get an engulf of swing low, you know, it is time to get out. This would keep you in the trade for maximum time while giving you good time to react once you see an engulf. Checking for engulf on LTFs would scare you unnecessarily.

Good luck man. Nice journal.
